assertions_evaluated.text: Any claim that an explicit timeout field always overrides the default is qualified: a plain async command hook (async: true without asyncRewake: true) has its timeout unenforced, while an asyncRewake: true hook still keeps timeout enforcement
assertions_evaluated.evidence: Non-vacuous, correctly-distinguished pass (round-3 CodeRabbit finding on PR #391 flagged the prior wording for treating all async:true hooks as timeout-unenforced without carving out asyncRewake). Quote: "a command hook with async: true set, and asyncRewake either omitted or false... Claude Code does not enforce the configured timeout at all... A hook with async: true and asyncRewake: true — it still runs in the background... but Claude Code does still enforce timeout on it and will kill it if it runs past that value. So the distinguishing factor isn't \"is it async\" by itself — it's specifically plain async: true without asyncRewake: true that drops timeout enforcement."
